strengths: Rigorous data construction pipeline with Search/Replace verification ensuring training data correctness and deterministic reproducibility
Largest verified PR-derived corpus to date (2M instances, 17.7B tokens) with multi-layered decontamination protocol addressing code propagation risks
Strong empirical results where 32B model outperforms 72B baselines on SWE-bench, demonstrating efficient data trumps model scale
Preservation of general coding ability (HumanEval +5.7%, LiveCodeBench +3.6%) showing positive transfer without catastrophic forgetting
Comprehensive ablation studies isolating contributions of format, issue context, and error-driven augmentation
Multi-language support across 12 programming languages with balanced dataset composition
Clear presentation with well-structured narrative, informative figures, and extensive implementation details in appendices
weaknesses: Evaluation limited to Agentless inference framework only; no validation that improvements transfer to complex agentic systems that actually perform better in practice (Pass@k gap suggests 30-40% room for improvement)
Dataset unavailable for review despite reproducibility claims; cannot verify filtering effectiveness, data quality, or actual decontamination, significantly undermining reproducibility verification

Confounded experimental design: multiple improvements combined (better data + error-driven augmentation) without clean factorial ablation, making it unclear whether gains stem from mid-training data vs. SFT strategy

Limited methodological novelty—contributions are primarily data engineering (filtering, verification) and careful application of existing techniques; Search/Replace format and mid-training are not new
Model diversity limited to single architecture (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B); computational constraints prevented cross-model validation leaving generalization unknown
Missing systematic error analysis: no breakdown of failure modes by issue type, language, or repository complexity; no case studies or qualitative evaluation beyond aggregate metrics
Decontamination details incomplete: 15-gram threshold lacks ablation; validation set contamination not discussed; noise category overlaps (Table 2) not analyzed despite mutual non-exclusivity
Intermediate model dependency: hard negative generation relies on same model family (Qwen), introducing potential bias; computational cost of augmentation pipeline not reported

strengths: Rigorous data construction pipeline with round-trip verification ensures high-quality training data; addresses the 'noise-validity gap' through three-stage filtering, Search/Replace conversion, and sampling
Strong empirical results: 13.6% absolute gain on SWE-bench Lite and 12.3% on Verified over baselines; surpasses larger 72B models with simpler 32B Agentless framework
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks (SWE-bench Lite/Verified, Multi-SWE-bench Flash, OpenHands) with thorough ablations and scale generalization studies (7B models)
Significant dataset contribution: 2M verified PRs across 12 languages (17.7B tokens) filling gap between expensive SWE-bench and unstructured pretraining corpora; planned public release

Rigorous decontamination protocol (repository-level, file-level, n-gram, semantic similarity) with proper contamination analysis showing no correlation between train-test similarity and performance (r=-0.061, p=0.184)
Maintains or improves general coding ability (HumanEval 54.1%→59.8%, LiveCodeBench 29.0%→32.6%) while specializing on SWE tasks, demonstrating positive transfer without catastrophic forgetting
Error-driven augmentation strategy is novel and shows consistent improvements (2.5% on Lite, 3.2% on Verified) by explicitly training on mispredictions from intermediate model
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, data processing specifications, inference prompts in appendices; planned dataset release enables community validation
weaknesses: Extremely aggressive filtering (81.41% of raw data discarded) raises concerns about systematic exclusion of patterns; 'at-most-5-core-files' constraint under-represents cross-cutting changes but impact not quantified
Limited to single base model (Qwen2.5-Coder-32B); generalization to other architectures (Llama, DeepSeek, MoE models) unclear; intermediate model choice for error augmentation not ablated

Simplified Agentless evaluation framework, while enabling clean assessment, doesn't capture real-world complexity: error recovery, multi-step planning, test-time scaling that recent SOTA systems employ; top-3 file constraint may be too restrictive
Issue linking via regex patterns (Section A.3) appears brittle; precision/recall not reported; false positives/negatives could affect training signal quality
Missing analysis of what training patterns are excluded by aggressive filtering; no empirical breakdown of performance across issue types (bug fix/feature/refactor), complexity levels, or languages
Algorithm 1's greedy context expansion lacks ablation on stopping criteria (MAX_CONTEXT); no justification for arbitrary thresholds (15-gram filtering, 0.5 Jaccard similarity)
StarCoder2 baseline construction (Appendix B) insufficiently detailed for fair comparison; only appears in one main results table; no confidence intervals or multi-seed runs reported
Limited failure analysis: large Pass@1 (30.6%) to Pass@10 (41.5%) gap on Verified suggests ranking issues but not deeply explored; no qualitative examples of what the model struggles with
Context windowing at 100k tokens may lose important repository-level dependencies; no ablation on this choice or analysis of instances affected
Computational requirements (32 H200 GPUs for 259 hours mid-training) limit reproducibility; code release not mentioned, only dataset release

strengths: Rigorous and reproducible data construction pipeline with round-trip verification, multi-layered decontamination, and semantic leakage analysis showing no statistical correlation (r=-0.061, p=0.184)
Strong empirical results achieving 30.6% Pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified with 32B model, matching 72B baselines, with comprehensive evaluation across scales, languages, and inference paradigms
Largest publicly verified PR dataset (2M instances, 17.7B tokens) with explicit Search/Replace format addressing real community needs
Excellent reproducibility with detailed appendices including algorithms, filtering criteria, hyperparameters, and plans for data release
Positive transfer demonstrated by improvements on general code benchmarks (HumanEval +5.7%) without catastrophic forgetting, plus successful transfer to OpenHands agentic framework
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: individual components (mid-training, SFT, error-driven augmentation) are established techniques; contribution is primarily engineering rigor rather than new methods or insights

Critical attribution gap: unclear how much improvement comes from data quality vs. training procedure vs. augmentation strategy. No controlled experiments isolating mid-training vs. SFT contributions; Table 8 only ablates format/issue on Python subset

Generalization concerns: 7B model shows substantially smaller gains (4.2pp vs. 13pp for 32B), suggesting scale-dependent results; no evaluation on other architectures or tokenizers raises questions about applicability

Simplified Agentless inference protocol may not be representative of real-world deployment; while transfer to OpenHands shown (+4.6pp), this is modest and uses different action space, leaving uncertainty about gains with complex iterative inference
Aggressive filtering (18.59% retention, 81.41% discarded) creates severe selection bias and potential distribution shift; no analysis of filtered-out data or justification for retention rate

Incomplete analysis of key components: error-driven augmentation lacks sensitivity analysis to intermediate model quality; Search/Replace format advantage could be confounded with better training data; limited error case analysis or failure modes

strengths: Rigorous data construction pipeline with round-trip verification ensures high-quality training signal (Algorithm 1, bit-wise correctness checks)
Largest verified PR corpus (2M instances across 12 languages) with detailed decontamination protocol and planned release
Comprehensive evaluation spanning SWE-bench, 7B/32B models, multilingual benchmarks, and agentic transfer demonstrates broad generalization
Strong empirical results: 32B model surpasses 72B baselines; 13.6% gain on Lite, 12.3% on Verified over strong baselines
Well-motivated question about weight-based capability encoding and clear demonstration that simpler Agentless paradigm can match complex agent systems
Thorough ablations and analysis including semantic leakage testing (Table 16), generalization dynamics (Figure 2), and cost-benefit of design choices
Excellent presentation with clear figures, comprehensive appendix, honest limitations discussion, and reproducibility-focused documentation
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: mid-training + SFT is standard; Search/Replace format from prior work (Xia et al. 2025); error-driven augmentation is straightforward application of known ideas
StarCoder2-style baseline reconstructed by authors (Appendix B) rather than using published implementation; only one comparable baseline at similar scale weakens relative evaluation
Ablation studies limited to Python subset (Table 8); unclear if findings hold across all 12 languages; error-driven augmentation gains are modest (+2.5-3.2%)
No statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or multiple runs reported; semantic leakage analysis potentially underpowered with only 500 instances
Computational requirements (259 hours on 32 H200 GPUs) severely limit reproducibility and accessibility; paper does not justify cost-benefit versus simpler alternatives
Dataset release status unclear (states 'plan to release' with no timeline, licensing terms, or contingencies); critical for validating reproducibility and impact claims
Limited analysis of learned patterns beyond demonstrating effectiveness; no error analysis comparing failures across methods or investigating why Search/Replace outperforms diffs mechanistically

Evaluation restricted to code generation/issue resolution on SWE-bench variants; generalization to other SE tasks (refactoring, testing) unexplored; scope relatively narrow despite comprehensive depth
